cells.tense: You are here with the pen, tending the feeling between people as it actually is.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: In your next hard conversation, take the weight of what they show you the way a builder takes stone — solid, nothing bent — then set it back down and step away.
cells.core:
In this room, you keep the space between people from going under. You notice what someone is feeling before they say it, and you stay with it without making it yours. Right now that works, and the ones close to you can feel it.

That skill is real, and it's also what keeps you standing in half-lit places, one step showing at a time. The next thing is to give it something solid to stand on. When something heavy comes up between you and someone else, take the weight the way a builder takes stone — carrying it clean, without bending it — then set it back down and step away. The road is more walkable that way, and you don't have to take the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what people feel, and it doesn't take you under.
cells.verb: tending the space where feeling between people can be held without anyone going under
cells.place: the half-lit stretch where one step shows at a time and the whole road cannot be seen

cells.tense: You'll be braced for what hasn't happened yet, packing feelings that aren't in the room.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Look at the oldest worry you're still packing about someone. If it's finished, set that piece down and keep only what's true today.
cells.core:
Somewhere in the half-lit stretch, you've started packing feelings that aren't here yet. You're bracing for how a conversation might go, pre-loading what someone might feel, and bearing it has tipped into gripping. The ones close to you can sense the pressure, and the road is being imagined step by step rather than walked.

Underneath the bracing is something living that hasn't been given room to end. Take the oldest worry still riding with you and ask whether it's finished. If it is, set that piece down and keep only what's true today. The clearing leaves space for the next step to actually show itself.

cells.tense: The door behind you was already closed, and you were still standing at it.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Name the true thing to the person you've been keeping it from, gently and once, and after that let it sit without repeating it.
cells.core:
In the half-lit stretch you've stopped holding the space, and the step you would take keeps not being taken. It looks like staying quiet where something needs to be said, and the room between you and others has gone thin. The knack is intact — it just isn't reaching across anymore.

What's missing is a clear word, tempered to what can be heard. Choose the person and the true thing you've been keeping back. Say it gently, once, and then leave it — no repeating, no softening it into fog. The energy that's been going into holding it back returns to you, and the next step shows up where the fog was.

cells.tense: You're already writing this room, and your hand is saying it belongs to someone else.
cells.ask: Map the next three moves that the feeling you're holding for someone actually calls for, and then make the first one.
cells.core:
Somewhere in the half-lit stretch, you've been quietly steering the space for people, and your version has it as something you're just getting through. You see what's needed between them before anyone says it, and you act on it. Your hand is on it; you'd say it isn't.

Underneath the carried feeling is something clean and quick. Take what you've been holding for someone else, line up the next three moves it needs, and make the first. The fog thins, and your footprints show up where you'd been saying you'd only passed through. You can still hold the space; this just puts your hand back on the pen.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is the Balanced cell's picture of a group check-in where the lone voice is weighed — the record supports the signature holding space for feeling without drowning in it, but not this scene. A reader could reasonably say the group version is not what is happening, so the ask will also be offered as something usable in one ordinary conversation between two people. The ask still teaches the person one concrete action, so it survives being wrong about them; if the read misses, they have still done a small act of holding. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line implying a group always has such a moment — better left out than said.
